external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A user's browser that communicates with the web application.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

processes.name: web application
processes.description: A web application that receives browser traffic and places jobs onto a message queue.
processes.source_excerpt: Web application with a queue-decoupled background process.

processes.name: background worker
processes.description: A background worker process that picks up jobs and performs the work.
processes.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_stores.name: message queue
data_stores.description: A queue onto which the web application puts jobs and from which the background worker picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue, and a background worker process picks them up and does the work.
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_stores.name: database
data_stores.description: A database read and written by the background worker that also stores the application's log records.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database. The database is also where we keep the application's log records.
data_stores.notes: The diagram does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: web application config
data_stores.description: A config store containing settings and the credentials needed by the web application, including its queue credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web application has a web application config
data_stores.notes: The config store holds the web application's queue credentials. The diagram does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: worker config
data_stores.description: A config store containing settings and the credentials needed by the worker, including its database credentials.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the worker has a worker config
data_stores.notes: The config store holds the worker's database credentials. The diagram does not say whether anything is encrypted at rest.

data_flows.name: talks to application
data_flows.description: The browser communicates with the web application.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A user's browser talks to the web application over HTTP/S across the public internet.

data_flows.name: puts jobs
data_flows.description: The web application places jobs onto the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It puts jobs onto a message queue
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the web application authenticates to the queue.

data_flows.name: picks up jobs
data_flows.description: The background worker picks jobs up from the message queue.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a background worker process picks them up and does the work.

data_flows.name: reads and writes
data_flows.description: The background worker reads from and writes to the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The background worker reads and writes the database.
data_flows.notes: The diagram does not say anything about how the worker authenticates to the database.

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The web application reads its settings from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: the web application has a web application config

data_flows.name: reads settings
data_flows.description: The background worker reads its settings from its config store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Both processes read their settings from a config store: … the worker has a worker config.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet outside the system's network.

trust_boundaries.name: web tier
trust_boundaries.description: The web tier where the web application runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the web application runs in our web tier

trust_boundaries.name: backend tier
trust_boundaries.description: The backend tier containing the queue, worker, database and config stores behind the web tier.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The queue, the worker and the database are all in the backend tier, behind the web tier.

assumptions.basis: A user's browser communicates with it across the public internet.

assumptions.assumption: The background worker has internal exposure.
assumptions.basis: The worker is described as being in the backend tier behind the web tier.

assumptions.assumption: The web application config contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it holds the web application's queue credentials.

assumptions.assumption: The worker config contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it holds the worker's database credentials.
